findings.message: GO-02/IN-07 explicitly include `cli_driver` in the layers whose git command strings and failure-detection logic must be moved behind infrastructure semantics, but the acceptance checks here only grep `apps/cli` and `apps/cli-composition`. AC-06 proves `apps/cli` dispatches through `GitDriver`, but it does not deterministically assert that `apps/cli-driver` itself contains no direct git command literals or failure classification, so the `cli_driver` portion of the stated goal can pass unverified.
findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal

findings.message: D5-D9 split the new sync refactor across three ownership layers without choosing one coherent public contract. D5 introduces `sync_current_branch`/`SyncError` at the infrastructure boundary, D6 rehomes sync/pull separation into the `GitWorkflowService` port chain, and D8/D9 then move orchestration out of composition root and cli. As written, `spec.json` and the later type catalogue cannot derive a single API surface or error-mapping boundary for `git sync`, so implementers can satisfy the prose while wiring incompatible layers.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: T001 is attributed to `ExplicitTrackBranch`, `TrackBranchClaim`, and `BranchReaderPort`, but the task text explicitly says those reference-only entries are unchanged. Remove those attributions or the contract no longer matches the described edit scope.

T005 is attributed to `FileArgs`, `CommitFromFileArgs`, and `UnstageArgs`, but the task text says the `AddAll` / `AddFromFile` / `CommitFromFile` / `NoteFromFile` / `Unstage` variants keep their existing shape and tests. Those symbol attributions look inflated for the described change.

The `plan.summary` block is prose-heavy restatement of the upstream ADR/spec behavior (`bin/sotp git sync` semantics, hexagonal layering, D7/D8 rationale) instead of an executable plan. The impl-plan review policy only permits target + operation + anchor cite here, so this section should be collapsed into taskable edits rather than restating the design contract.

`T005` is attributed to `FileArgs`, `CommitFromFileArgs`, and `UnstageArgs`, but the task text only removes `SwitchAndPull`, adds `Sync`, and rewires the git-family dispatch path; it explicitly says the `AddAll` / `AddFromFile` / `CommitFromFile` / `NoteFromFile` / `Unstage` variants keep their existing shape. Those three catalog entries are therefore over-attributed and make the task-contract imply a broader edit than the plan actually describes.

S1-S7 (and the task bullets beneath them) restate upstream ADR/spec behavior in prose instead of staying in the executable-plan format. Examples include 'exact stdout/stderr/exit contracts', 'git pull --ff-only classified into 3 typed SyncError variants', and 'graceful skip forbidden'. The impl-plan prompt only allows target + operation + anchor cite, so this text needs to be collapsed into action items.

T002 over-attributes `BranchReaderPort` even though the task text explicitly says 'Reference-only entries (ExplicitTrackBranch, TrackBranchClaim, BranchReaderPort) are unchanged'. That catalogue entry is not part of the work and should be removed from the task-contract map.

AC-03 is mapped only to T005, but T006 explicitly owns deletion of `apps/cli-composition/src/git.rs` helpers `git_switch_and_pull_in` / `git_switch_and_pull_impl` in `impl-plan.json` line 36. AC-03 requires those symbols to be absent, so the load-bearing coverage is split incorrectly: T005 could be treated as covering AC-03 while the helper deletion is deferred to an unmapped task. Add T006 to AC-03 coverage or move that deletion fully into T005.

T009 includes `Add switch-and-pull grep assertion` without naming the target file, script, task, or symbol where that assertion should be added. The rest of T009 names files, but this persistent verification step lacks a target boundary, so an executor has to invent where it belongs.

AC-10/IN-11 require replacing the non-test `apps/cli/src/commands/track/branch_ops.rs` git判定/direct infrastructure path, but the plan never assigns that production edit. `task-coverage.json` maps AC-10 to T005/T006/T008, while T005 only covers `apps/cli/src/commands/git.rs`, T006 covers `apps/cli-composition`, and T008 mentions only `branch_ops.rs tests` cleanup. An implementer can follow all tasks and still leave the production `branch_ops.rs` rev-parse/GitRepository path outside the plan.

AC-09 is only mapped to T003, but T003 just adds the interactor types and mock-port tests; it does not migrate the live track/pr/review_v2 composition flows that AC-09 requires to be orchestrated through those interactors. The executable tasks that perform that migration are T006/T007, and T007 even cites AC-09 in impl-plan.json, so leaving AC-09 covered solely by T003 makes the coverage map report the acceptance criterion complete before the actual caller migration is covered.

Several `docs` fields in the new/modified catalog entries restate ADR/spec rationale instead of staying anchor-only, which violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`. The clearest instance is `usecase::git_workflow::DiagnosticText` at line 38, and the same pattern recurs in `GitWorkflowError`, `GitWorkflowInteractor`, `GitPrimitivePort`, `TrackArchiveFsPort`, `GitWorkflowService`, and the corresponding CLI/infrastructure entries: they explain why the design exists rather than just naming the changed surface and citing the anchors.

`contract-map.md` still renders `FsGitWorkflowAdapter` as implementing `GitWorkflowService`, but the catalogue declares that trait impl as `action: delete` and the replacement `GitPrimitivePort` impl as `action: add`. Because deleted `SwitchAndPullArgs` / `GitRepository` nodes are omitted from the map, this stale live edge makes the rendered type contract contradict the target-state catalogue and preserves the old adapter-to-application-service relationship in the PR-level view.

The `docs` field for `usecase::git_workflow::GitPrimitivePort` is restating the upstream contract in prose (per-method git semantics, explicit implementation target, and branch-root behavior) instead of staying at the required "change + operation + anchor cite" level. This violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`; the same pattern also appears in `cli::commands::git::GitCommand`, `cli_driver::git::GitInput`, and `cli_composition::git::GitCompositionRoot`.

`GitWorkflowService::current_branch_track_id` still returns `Result<Option<String>, GitWorkflowError>` here, so the service boundary exports a branch-derived track identifier as a raw string instead of a validated domain type. That keeps the track-id contract stringly typed and pushes re-validation onto every caller.

`domain-types.json` is missing the reference nodes needed by this track's usecase surface: `BranchReadError` (`usecase-types.json:555`), `domain::TrackId` (`:644`, `:656`, `:678`, `:702`, `:732`) and `domain::CommitHash` (`:302`, `:712`, `:733`, `:741`). Without those declarations, the contract map leaves the new cross-layer type edges unresolved.

`TrackGitInteractor` method docs restate upstream behavior contracts instead of only citing anchors: the catalogue spells out the branch-create sequence, switch-base sequence, archive rollback sequence, and stdout behavior. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` applies to `<layer>-types.json` docs/intent fields, so this creates a second behavioral source of truth that can drift from IN-05/IN-10/CN-03/AC-04. Replace the prose with target/operation plus anchor cites.

The PR/review interactor method docs also encode behavior flow details (`fetch_branch -> show_file_at_ref(...) -> raw JSON` and current-branch verification before resolving HEAD) rather than deferring to the cited spec anchors. This violates the same no-upstream-restatement rule for type catalogues and makes these usecase entries independent behavioral documentation instead of type contracts tied to IN-10/CN-03/AC-09.
